uncited: GPU Memory and Buffer Construction defines the mechanisms for organizing volumetric data, transfer functions, and rendering state into GPU-accessible memory structures (textures, framebuffers, and unified buffers) to enable efficient raycasting and volume visualization.

It solves the problem of translating host-side volumetric representations (dense grids, hexahedral meshes) into GPU-friendly formats that minimize memory bandwidth bottlenecks and support specific rendering techniques like MIP, speckle reduction, and hybrid rasterization-compositing.

It sets itself apart from [Volume Texture Creation](1857-volume-texture-creation.md) by focusing on the final memory layout, buffer construction, and resource management (framebuffers, unified buffers) rather than the interpolation or sampling logic itself.

The family shares the principle of mapping logical volumetric data structures to specific GPU memory resources (textures, framebuffers, or unified buffers) with strict constraints on data types, dimensions, and formats to ensure compatibility with shader pipelines.
*   1D Textures: For transfer functions (color and opacity).
*   2D Textures: For depth buffers, color buffers, noise textures, and specialized topology data (ClearView).
*   Framebuffer Objects (FBOs): For offscreen rendering and ping-pong accumulation.
*   Unified Buffers/Structs: For passing metadata and handles to kernels (CUDA).
The concepts in this family originate from CUDA-accelerated volume rendering engines and hybrid rendering pipelines.
These methods are used in scientific visualization, medical imaging, and real-time volume rendering applications where performance and memory efficiency are critical.
